messages:
mia: Heads-up — I'm proposing we switch to an adaptive min on-demand floor per AZ instead of a global flat floor. Spot churn has been asymmetric across AZs and we're overpaying in stable AZs. Thoughts?

raj: +1 to trying it, but need to be careful about network hotspots and cross-AZ egress when we pull workloads off spot.

sam: Can you sketch the rules? e.g., how do we compute the floor in runtime?

mia: Rough idea: base_floor per tenant (defaults) then add AZ risk multiplier based on recent uninterrupted time and spot eviction rate. If eviction_rate > threshold -> bump floor. Also cap bump to avoid full on-demand conversion.

leah: We also need safe fallback routing so we don't route a request across region boundaries for low-latency workloads. Some models (chat-critical) must prefer same-AZ on-demand first.

infra-bot: Alert: us-west2-a spot eviction rate 18% over last 24h, average reconnect latency 420ms.

raj: ok, so algorithm sketch:

```
# per AZ
effective_floor = max(global_min, base_floor, ceil(eviction_rate * scaling_factor * demand))
effective_floor = min(effective_floor, max_on_demand_cap)
```

Then routing will enforce: prefer local on-demand if available up to effective_floor, otherwise best-effort spot.

sam: What signals go into eviction_rate? raw preempt counts? normalized by capacity-hours? Need to avoid noise from short blips.

mia: Use exponential moving avg of preemptions per instance-hour and a hazard window (24h). Also incorporate network incidents: if AZ has >X packet drop or inter-AZ egress spike, treat as elevated risk.

leah: Cost projection please — if us-west2-a goes from 10% to 25% floor, what delta on monthly bill? We should simulate 7d traces before the rollout.

mia: I'll run a simulation job: mirror the autoscale traces and calculate on-demand-hours under different floor policies. Expected: <6% overall cost increase but 30% fewer interruption events for critical jobs.

raj: One more safety net: introduce "interruption credits" per tenant. When we evict a spot task due to reclaim, deduct credits; if credits below threshold, scheduler prefers on-demand for that tenant until credits recover. Helps multi-tenant fairness.

sam: Nice. Implementation notes: scheduler needs an AZ-local allocation path and a cross-AZ fallback path. Cross-AZ fallback must annotate requests with egress budget and latency SLO. If egress > budget, refuse fallback and instead queue briefly or use degraded model.

mia: We'll also add a small hysteresis window to avoid flipping floors every hour. Update cadence = 6h by default, can reduce to 1h in high-variance AZs.

leah: For rollout plan: canary in us-west2-a (high evictions) and eu-central1-b (historically stable) so we can see cost/eviction delta both ways. 2-week canary, telemetry dashboards + alerts for 2x baseline eviction reduction or >5% cost increase.

mia: Owners: I'll run simulation and build config PR. @sam will prototype scheduler changes. @raj handle the routing policy and safe-fallback policy. @leah will own cost sims and dashboards.

sam: Implementation question — do we store per-AZ floor in config DB or compute on the fly in autoscaler? I vote compute and persist snapshot every 6h to make changes auditable.

raj: Persisted snapshots make incident debugging easier. +1.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4123: "Adaptive AZ min-on-demand floor proto + canary" assigned to mia, sam, raj, leah.

mia: Ok I'll open the PR with config schema and simulation results by EOD tomorrow, then scheduling prototype next week. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
